data.one_liner: Run multiple future-returning and async functions with limited concurrency.
data.what_it_does: It provides a mechanism to limit the concurrency of asynchronous operations in Dart. You can wrap future-returning functions with a limiter to ensure only a specified number of them run simultaneously.
use_when: You need to process a large list of async tasks without overwhelming system resources or rate limits.
You want a direct Dart port of the popular JavaScript p-limit library.
avoid_when: You need a fully featured thread pool or complex task queue implementation.
You require passing arguments directly into the queue wrapper function without wrapping them in closures.
weaknesses: Lacks advanced queue options like task priorities or thread pools.
Does not inherently support passing separate arguments to functions without closures.

alternatives.name: async
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides core utility functions and collections for asynchronous programming in Dart, including some queuing primitives.
